$$ \mathbf{u}_{t}^{M}=M_{0}\mathbf{y}_{t}^{\sf nat}+\sum_{i=1}^{\tilde{h}}\lambda_{i}^{1/4}M_{i}Y_{t-1:t-\tilde{m}}^{\sf nat}\boldsymbol{\varphi}_{i}, $$

where $(\lambda_{i},\boldsymbol{\varphi}_{i})$ are the top $\tilde{h}$ eigenpairs of the Hankel matrix $H\in\mathbb{R}^{\tilde{m}\times\tilde{m}}$ with $H_{ij}=\frac{(1-\tilde{\gamma})^{i+j-1}}{i+j-1}$ , such that

$$ \sum_{t=1}^{T}\left|c_{t}(\mathbf{y}_{t}^{M},\mathbf{u}_{t}^{M})-c_{t}(\mathbf{y}_{t}^{K},\mathbf{u}_{t}^{K})\right|\leq 2\varepsilon T, $$

provided

$$ \tilde{m}\geq\frac{1}{\tilde{\gamma}}\log\left(\frac{6\tilde{G}\tilde{\kappa}^{14}\tilde{\kappa}_{B}^{3}\tilde{\kappa}_{C}^{5}\tilde{W}^{2}}{\varepsilon\tilde{\gamma}^{5}}\right),\quad\tilde{h}\geq 2\log T\cdot\log\left(\frac{400\tilde{G}\tilde{\kappa}^{14}\tilde{\kappa}_{B}^{3}\tilde{\kappa}_{C}^{5}\tilde{W}^{2}\sqrt{\tilde{m}}d}{\varepsilon\tilde{\gamma}^{9/2}}\log T\log^{1/4}\left(\frac{2}{\tilde{\gamma}}\right)\right). $$

Moreover, the parameters $M$ lie in the bounded set

$$ \mathcal{K}=\left\{M\in\mathbb{R}^{\tilde{h}\times n\times p}\;\middle|\;\|\mathbf{y}_{t}^{M}\|,\|\mathbf{u}_{t}^{M}\|\leq\frac{4\tilde{\kappa}^{6}\tilde{\kappa}_{B}\tilde{\kappa}_{C}^{2}\tilde{W}}{\tilde{\gamma}^{2}},\ \|M_{0}\|\leq\tilde{\kappa},\ \|M_{i}\|\leq\tilde{\kappa}^{4}\tilde{\kappa}_{B}\tilde{\kappa}_{C}\sqrt{\frac{2}{\tilde{\gamma}}}\right\}. $$

Thus, we complete the proof of Lemma 4.2 as follows:

#### Proof of Lemma 4.2.

Substituting the values of the bounds in Lemma A.3 and substituting $\varepsilon=1/\sqrt{T}$ completes the proof. ∎

### A.1 Approximating LDC with spectral Surrogate Controller

In this section, we prove Lemma A.2. We begin by deriving bounds on the observations and controls generated by any linear dynamic controller in $\mathcal{S}$ , as well as by the corresponding spectral-projection linear controller constructed in Lemma A.2. These bounds are established in the following lemmas.

#### Lemma A.4.

Let $(A_{\pi},B_{\pi},C_{\pi})\in\mathcal{S}$ . Then for all $t\geq 0$ , the observation and control satisfy:

$$ \|\mathbf{y}_{t}^{\pi}\|,\|\mathbf{u}_{t}^{\pi}\|\leq\frac{\kappa_{C}\kappa^{3}W}{\gamma}. $$

#### Proof.

Define the joint state $\mathbf{z}_{t}^{\pi}=\begin{bmatrix}\mathbf{x}_{t}^{\pi}\\ \mathbf{s}_{t}^{\pi}\end{bmatrix}$ , with closed-loop dynamics

$$ \mathbf{z}_{t+1}^{\pi}=\mathcal{A}\mathbf{z}_{t}^{\pi}+\mathcal{B}\mathbf{w}_{t},\quad\text{where}\quad\mathcal{A}=\begin{bmatrix}A&BC_{\pi}\\
B_{\pi}C&A_{\pi}\end{bmatrix},\quad\mathcal{B}=\begin{bmatrix}I\\
0\end{bmatrix}. $$

Since $\mathbf{z}_{0}^{\pi}=0$ , we have

$$ \mathbf{z}_{t}^{\pi}=\sum_{i=0}^{t-1}\mathcal{A}^{t-1-i}\mathcal{B}\mathbf{w}_{i}. $$

The outputs are $\mathbf{y}_{t}^{\pi}=[C\;\;0]\mathbf{z}_{t}^{\pi}$ , $\mathbf{u}_{t}^{\pi}=[0\;\;C_{\pi}]\mathbf{z}_{t}^{\pi}$ . Using definition 3.4, $\|\mathcal{A}^{i}\|\leq\kappa^{2}(1-\gamma)^{i}$ , $\|\mathcal{B}\|=1$ , $\|C\|\leq\kappa_{C}$ , $\|C_{\pi}\|\leq\kappa$ , and $\|\mathbf{w}_{i}\|\leq W$ , we get:

$$ \|\mathbf{y}_{t}^{\pi}\|\leq\kappa_{C}\sum_{i=0}^{t-1}\|\mathcal{A}^{i}\|W\leq\frac{\kappa^{2}\kappa_{C}W}{\gamma},\quad\|\mathbf{u}_{t}^{\pi}\|\leq\kappa\sum_{i=0}^{t-1}\|\mathcal{A}^{i}\|W\leq\frac{\kappa^{3}W}{\gamma}. $$

∎

#### Lemma A.5.

Let $(A_{\pi},B_{\pi},C_{\pi})\in\mathcal{S}$ and let $K$ be as mentioned in Lemma A.2 for $(A_{\pi},B_{\pi},C_{\pi})$ . Then, for any $t\geq 0$ ,

$$ \left\lVert\mathbf{y}_{t}^{K}\right\rVert\leq\frac{\kappa^{2}\kappa_{C}W}{\gamma}\,. $$

#### Proof.

Observe that our spectral-projection linear controller can be represented by the lifted system defined in Equations (7), (8), (9) and (10) for the choice of $K_{i}$ in Lemma A.2. By definition 3.4, $\tilde{A}+\tilde{B}\tilde{K}\tilde{C}=HLH^{-1}$ , and thus $\left\lVert(\tilde{A}+\tilde{B}\tilde{K}\tilde{C})^{i}\right\rVert\leq\kappa^{2}(1-\gamma)^{i}$ . Moreover, observe that $\left\lVert\tilde{\mathbf{w}}_{t}\right\rVert\leq W$ . Thus,

$$ \tilde{\mathbf{x}}_{t}^{K}=\sum_{i=1}^{t}(\tilde{A}+\tilde{B}\tilde{K}\tilde{C})^{i-1}\tilde{\mathbf{w}}_{t-i}\implies\left\lVert\tilde{\mathbf{x}}_{t}^{K}\right\rVert\leq\frac{\kappa^{2}W}{\gamma}\,. $$

Using Eqn (11), it is clear that $\mathbf{y}_{t}^{K}=\begin{bmatrix}C&0&\dots&0\end{bmatrix}\tilde{\mathbf{x}}_{t}^{K}$ and thus, $\left\lVert\mathbf{y}_{t}^{K}\right\rVert\leq\frac{\kappa^{2}\kappa_{C}W}{\gamma}$ ∎

We now complete the proof of Lemma A.2 as follows:

#### Proof of Lemma A.2.

Observe that

$$ \mathbf{u}_{t}^{\pi}=\sum_{i=0}^{t}C_{\pi}A_{\pi}^{i}B_{\pi}\mathbf{y}_{t-i}^{\pi}\,. $$

Consider the following policy $\pi_{\tau}$ defined for some $\tau\in\mathbb{N}\cup\{0\}$ :

$$ \mathbf{u}_{t}^{\pi_{\tau}}=\begin{cases}\sum_{i=0}^{h}\sigma_{i}^{1/4}K_{i}Y^{\pi_{\tau}}_{t:t-m}\boldsymbol{\phi}_{i}&\text{if }t\leq\tau-1\\
\sum_{i=0}^{m}C_{\pi}A_{\pi}^{i}B_{\pi}\mathbf{y}_{t-i}^{\pi_{\tau}}&\text{if }t=\tau\\
\sum_{i=0}^{t}C_{\pi}A_{\pi}^{i}B_{\pi}\mathbf{y}_{t-i}^{\pi_{\tau}}&\text{if }t\geq\tau+1\end{cases} $$

Observe that $\pi_{0}$ is pure LDC policy and that $\pi_{T+1}$ is purely spectral policy. In order to bound the difference of costs between these, we shall bound the difference of costs between $\pi_{\tau}$ and $\pi_{\tau-1}$ for any $\tau\in[T]$ .

Observe that for all $t\in[0,\tau-2]$ , $\mathbf{u}_{t}^{\pi_{\tau}}=\mathbf{u}_{t}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}$ and for all $t\in[0,\tau-1]$ , $\mathbf{y}_{t}^{\pi_{\tau}}=\mathbf{y}_{t}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}$ by the definition of $\pi_{\tau}$ . Thus, $Y^{\pi_{\tau}}_{\tau-1:\tau-m-1}=Y^{\pi_{\tau-1}}_{\tau-1:\tau-m-1}$ and this gives us

$$ \displaystyle\mathbf{u}_{\tau-1}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}=\sum_{i=1}^{m}C_{\pi}A_{\pi}^{i}B_{\pi}\mathbf{y}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}_{\tau-i-1}=\sum_{i=0}^{m}C_{\pi}H_{\pi}L_{\pi}^{i}H_{\pi}^{-1}B_{\pi}\mathbf{y}_{\tau-i-1}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}\,. $$

Writing $L_{\pi}^{i}=\sum_{j=1}^{d}\alpha_{j}^{i}e_{j}e_{j}^{\top}$ , and defining $\mu_{\alpha}=\begin{bmatrix}1&\alpha&\dots&\alpha^{m}\end{bmatrix}^{\top}\in{\mathbb{R}}^{m+1}$ , we get

$$ \displaystyle\mathbf{u}_{\tau-1}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}=\sum_{i=0}^{m}C_{\pi}H_{\pi}\left(\sum_{j=1}^{d}\alpha_{j}^{i}e_{j}e_{j}^{\top}\right)H_{\pi}^{-1}B_{\pi}\mathbf{y}_{\tau-i-1}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}=\sum_{j=1}^{d}C_{\pi}H_{\pi}e_{j}e_{j}^{\top}H_{\pi}^{-1}B_{\pi}Y^{\pi_{\tau-1}}_{\tau-1:\tau-m-1}\mu_{\alpha_{j}}\,. $$

Since $\{\boldsymbol{\phi}_{i}\,|\,i\in[m]\cup\{0\}\}$ form an orthonormal basis,

$$ \displaystyle\mathbf{u}_{\tau-1}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}=\sum_{j=1}^{d}C_{\pi}H_{\pi}e_{j}e_{j}^{\top}H_{\pi}^{-1}B_{\pi}Y^{\pi_{\tau-1}}_{\tau-1:\tau-m-1}\left(\sum_{i=0}^{m}\boldsymbol{\phi}_{i}\boldsymbol{\phi}_{i}^{\top}\right)\mu_{\alpha_{j}}=\sum_{i=0}^{m}\sigma_{i}^{1/4}K_{i}Y^{\pi_{\tau-1}}_{\tau-1:\tau-m-1}\boldsymbol{\phi}_{i}\,. $$

Since, $Y^{\pi_{\tau-1}}_{\tau-1:\tau-m-1}=Y^{\pi_{\tau}}_{\tau-1:\tau-m-1}$ , and all of $\{\mathbf{y}_{t}^{\pi_{\tau}}\,|\,t\in[\tau-1]\}$ are outputs of the spectral-projection linear policy. Using Lemma A.5, we know that $\left\lVert Y^{\pi_{\tau}}_{\tau-1:\tau-m-1}\right\rVert\leq\frac{\sqrt{m+1}\kappa^{2}\kappa_{C}W}{\gamma}\leq\frac{2\kappa^{2}\kappa_{C}W\sqrt{m}}{\gamma}$ . Moreover,

$$ \mathbf{u}_{t}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}=\sum_{i=0}^{m}\sigma_{i}^{1/4}K_{i}Y^{\pi_{\tau}}_{\tau-1:\tau-m-1}\boldsymbol{\phi}_{i}\,. $$

Taking the difference, we get that:

$$ \displaystyle\left\lVert\mathbf{u}_{\tau-1}^{\pi_{\tau}}-\mathbf{u}_{\tau-1}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}\right\rVert\leq\sum_{i=h+1}^{m}\left\lVert\sigma_{i}^{1/4}K_{i}\right\rVert\left\lVert Y^{\pi_{\tau}}_{\tau-1:\tau-m-1}\right\rVert\leq\frac{2\kappa^{6}\kappa_{C}W\sqrt{m}}{\gamma}\sum_{i=h+1}^{m}\sum_{j=1}^{d}|\boldsymbol{\phi}_{i}^{\top}\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\alpha_{j}}| $$

Using Lemma 7.4 of [7], we get that:

$$ \displaystyle\left\lVert\mathbf{u}_{\tau-1}^{\pi_{\tau}}-\mathbf{u}_{\tau-1}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}\right\rVert \displaystyle\leq\frac{2\kappa^{6}\kappa_{C}Wd\sqrt{m}}{\gamma}\log^{1/4}\left(\frac{2}{\gamma}\right)\int_{h}^{\infty}\exp\left(-\frac{\pi^{2}j}{16\log T}\right)dj \displaystyle\leq\frac{4\kappa^{6}\kappa_{C}Wd\sqrt{m}}{\gamma}\log T\log^{1/4}\left(\frac{2}{\gamma}\right)\exp\left(-\frac{\pi^{2}h}{16\log T}\right) \displaystyle\leq\delta_{1}\quad\quad\quad\quad[h\geq 2\log T\log\left(\frac{4\kappa^{6}\kappa_{C}Wd\sqrt{m}}{\delta_{1}\gamma}\log T\log^{1/4}\left(\frac{2}{\gamma}\right)\right)] $$

Now, observe that since the controls of $\pi_{\tau}$ and $\pi_{\tau-1}$ are the same until time $\tau-2$ , $\mathbf{x}_{\tau-1}^{\pi_{\tau}}=\mathbf{x}_{\tau-1}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}$ . Thus, using eqn. (14), we get that:

$$ \displaystyle\left\lVert\mathbf{x}_{\tau}^{\pi_{\tau}}-\mathbf{x}_{\tau}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}\right\rVert=\left\lVert B(\mathbf{u}_{\tau-1}^{\pi_{\tau}}-\mathbf{u}_{\tau-1}^{\pi_{\tau-1}})\right\rVert\leq\kappa_{B}\delta_{1} $$

and

$$ \displaystyle\left\lVert\mathbf{y}_{\tau}^{\pi_{\tau}}-\mathbf{y}_{\tau}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}\right\rVert=\left\lVert CB(\mathbf{u}_{\tau-1}^{\pi_{\tau}}-\mathbf{u}_{\tau-1}^{\pi_{\tau-1}})\right\rVert\leq\kappa_{B}\kappa_{C}\delta_{1} $$

Again by using the fact that $\mathbf{y}^{\pi_{\tau}}_{t-i}=\mathbf{y}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}_{t-i}$ for all $i\geq 1$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\left\lVert\mathbf{u}^{\pi_{\tau}}_{\tau}-\mathbf{u}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}_{\tau}\right\rVert \displaystyle=\left\lVert\sum_{i=0}^{\tau}C_{\pi}A_{\pi}^{i}B_{\pi}\mathbf{y}_{\tau-i}^{\pi_{\tau}}-\sum_{i=0}^{m}C_{\pi}A_{\pi}^{i}B_{\pi}\mathbf{y}_{\tau-i}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}\right\rVert \displaystyle\leq\left\lVert C_{\pi}B_{\pi}\left(\mathbf{y}_{\tau}^{\pi_{\tau}}-\mathbf{y}_{\tau}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}\right)\right\rVert+\left\lVert\sum_{i=1}^{\tau}C_{\pi}A_{\pi}^{i}B_{\pi}\mathbf{y}_{\tau-i}^{\pi_{\tau}}-\sum_{i=1}^{m}C_{\pi}A_{\pi}^{i}B_{\pi}\mathbf{y}_{\tau-i}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}\right\rVert \displaystyle\leq\kappa_{B}\kappa_{C}\kappa^{2}\delta_{1}+\frac{\kappa^{6}\kappa_{C}W}{\gamma^{2}}\left(1-\gamma\right)^{m+1}\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad[\mbox{choice of }h] \displaystyle\leq 2\kappa^{2}\kappa_{B}\kappa_{C}\delta_{1}\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad[m\geq\frac{1}{\gamma}\log\left(\frac{\kappa^{4}W}{\kappa_{B}\gamma^{2}\delta_{1}}\right)] $$

Now, for any $t>\tau$ , we have that

$$ \displaystyle\begin{bmatrix}\mathbf{x}_{t}^{\pi_{\tau}}-\mathbf{x}_{t}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}\\[4.0pt]
\mathbf{s}_{t}^{\pi_{\tau}}-\mathbf{s}_{t}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}A&B_{\pi}C\\[4.0pt]
BC_{\pi}&A_{\pi}\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}\mathbf{x}_{t-1}^{\pi_{\tau}}-\mathbf{x}_{t-1}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}\\[4.0pt]
\mathbf{s}_{t-1}^{\pi_{\tau}}-\mathbf{s}_{t-1}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}A&B_{\pi}C\\[4.0pt]
BC_{\pi}&A_{\pi}\end{bmatrix}^{t-\tau-1}\begin{bmatrix}\mathbf{x}_{\tau+1}^{\pi_{\tau}}-\mathbf{x}_{\tau+1}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}\\[4.0pt]
\mathbf{s}_{\tau+1}^{\pi_{\tau}}-\mathbf{s}_{\tau+1}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}\end{bmatrix}\,. $$

In order to compute the terms on the RHS,

$$ \displaystyle\left\lVert\mathbf{x}_{\tau+1}^{\pi_{\tau}}-\mathbf{x}_{\tau+1}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}\right\rVert \displaystyle=\left\lVert A\left(\mathbf{x}_{\tau}^{\pi_{\tau}}-\mathbf{x}_{\tau}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}\right)+B\left(\mathbf{u}^{\pi_{\tau}}_{\tau}-\mathbf{u}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}_{\tau}\right)\right\rVert \displaystyle\leq\kappa^{2}\left\lVert\mathbf{x}_{\tau}^{\pi_{\tau}}-\mathbf{x}_{\tau}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}\right\rVert+\kappa_{B}\left\lVert\mathbf{u}^{\pi_{\tau}}_{\tau}-\mathbf{u}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}_{\tau}\right\rVert \displaystyle\leq\kappa^{2}\kappa_{B}\delta_{1}+2\kappa^{2}\kappa_{B}^{2}\kappa_{C}\delta_{1}\leq 3\kappa^{2}\kappa_{B}^{2}\kappa_{C}\delta_{1}\,.\quad\quad[\mbox{Eqns \eqref{eq:x_tau_bound} and \eqref{eq:u_tau_bound}}] $$

and thus,

$$ \displaystyle\left\lVert\mathbf{y}_{\tau+1}^{\pi_{\tau}}-\mathbf{y}_{\tau+1}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}\right\rVert=\left\lVert C(\mathbf{x}_{\tau+1}^{\pi_{\tau}}-\mathbf{x}_{\tau+1}^{\pi_{\tau-1}})\right\rVert\leq 3\kappa^{2}\kappa_{B}^{2}\kappa_{C}^{2}\delta_{1} $$

Moreover, for $t>\tau$ , the controller does behave like an LDC, however, the starting state is different and must be calculated. Observe that if $\mathbf{s}_{t}^{\pi_{\tau}}:=\sum_{i=0}^{t}A_{\pi}^{i}B_{\pi}\mathbf{y}_{t-i}^{\pi_{\tau}}$ for all $t>\tau$ , then the control is correctly defined. Hence,

$$ \displaystyle\left\lVert\mathbf{s}_{\tau+1}^{\pi_{\tau}}-\mathbf{s}_{\tau+1}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}\right\rVert \displaystyle=\left\lVert A_{\pi}B_{\pi}\left(\mathbf{y}_{\tau}^{\pi_{\tau}}-\mathbf{y}_{\tau}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}\right)+B_{\pi}\left(\mathbf{y}_{\tau+1}^{\pi_{\tau}}-\mathbf{y}_{\tau+1}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}\right)\right\rVert \displaystyle\leq\kappa^{3}\kappa_{B}\kappa_{C}\delta_{1}+3\kappa^{3}\kappa_{B}^{2}\kappa_{C}^{2}\delta_{1}\leq 4\kappa^{3}\kappa_{B}^{2}\kappa_{C}^{2}\delta_{1}\quad\quad\quad\quad[\mbox{Eqns \eqref{eq:y_tau_bound} and \eqref{eq:y_tau+1_bound}}]\,. $$

Putting this together, we have that

$$ \displaystyle\left\lVert\begin{bmatrix}\mathbf{x}_{\tau+1}^{\pi_{\tau}}-\mathbf{x}_{\tau+1}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}\\[4.0pt]
\mathbf{s}_{\tau+1}^{\pi_{\tau}}-\mathbf{s}_{\tau+1}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}\end{bmatrix}\right\rVert \displaystyle\leq 3\kappa^{2}\kappa_{B}^{2}\kappa_{C}\delta_{1}+4\kappa^{3}\kappa_{B}^{2}\kappa_{C}^{2}\delta_{1}\leq 7\kappa^{3}\kappa_{B}^{2}\kappa_{C}^{2}\delta_{1}\,. $$

Thus, we have

$$ \displaystyle\left\lVert\begin{bmatrix}\mathbf{x}_{t}^{\pi_{\tau}}-\mathbf{x}_{t}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}\\[4.0pt]
\mathbf{s}_{t}^{\pi_{\tau}}-\mathbf{s}_{t}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}\end{bmatrix}\right\rVert \displaystyle\leq\kappa^{2}\left(1-\gamma\right)^{t-\tau-1}\left\lVert\begin{bmatrix}\mathbf{x}_{\tau+1}^{\pi_{\tau}}-\mathbf{x}_{\tau+1}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}\\[4.0pt]
\mathbf{s}_{\tau+1}^{\pi_{\tau}}-\mathbf{s}_{\tau+1}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}\end{bmatrix}\right\rVert\leq 7\kappa^{5}\kappa_{B}^{2}\kappa_{C}^{2}\delta_{1}\,. $$

Observe that

$$ \mathbf{y}_{t}^{\pi_{\tau}}-\mathbf{y}_{t}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}=\begin{bmatrix}C&0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}\mathbf{x}_{t}^{\pi_{\tau}}-\mathbf{x}_{t}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}\\[4.0pt]
\mathbf{s}_{t}^{\pi_{\tau}}-\mathbf{s}_{t}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}\end{bmatrix}\,,\quad\quad\mathbf{y}_{t}^{\pi_{\tau}}-\mathbf{y}_{t}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}=\begin{bmatrix}0&C_{\pi}\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}\mathbf{x}_{t}^{\pi_{\tau}}-\mathbf{x}_{t}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}\\[4.0pt]
\mathbf{s}_{t}^{\pi_{\tau}}-\mathbf{s}_{t}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}\end{bmatrix}\,, $$

for all $t>\tau$ . Thus, for all $t>\tau$ (and also for all $t\in[T]$ using the previous bounds) we have that

$$ \displaystyle\max\left\{\left\lVert\mathbf{y}_{t}^{\pi_{\tau}}-\mathbf{y}_{t}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}\right\rVert,\left\lVert\mathbf{u}_{t}^{\pi_{\tau}}-\mathbf{u}_{t}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}\right\rVert\right\}\leq 7\kappa^{6}\kappa_{B}^{2}\kappa_{C}^{3}\delta_{1}\,. $$

Now, observe that:

$$ \displaystyle\max\left\{\left\lVert\mathbf{y}_{t}^{\pi_{T+1}}-\mathbf{y}_{t}^{\pi_{0}}\right\rVert,\left\lVert\mathbf{u}_{t}^{\pi_{T+1}}-\mathbf{u}_{t}^{\pi_{0}}\right\rVert\right\} \displaystyle\leq\sum_{\tau=1}^{T+1}\max\left\{\left\lVert\mathbf{y}_{t}^{\pi_{\tau}}-\mathbf{y}_{t}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}\right\rVert,\left\lVert\mathbf{u}_{t}^{\pi_{\tau}}-\mathbf{u}_{t}^{\pi_{\tau-1}}\right\rVert\right\} \displaystyle\leq 14\kappa^{6}\kappa_{B}^{2}\kappa_{C}^{3}\delta_{1}T $$

If out choice of $\delta_{1}\leq W/14\kappa^{3}\kappa_{B}^{2}\kappa_{C}^{2}\gamma T$ , then the difference is upper bounded by $\kappa^{3}\kappa_{C}W/\gamma$ and since by lemma A.4, $\left\lVert\mathbf{y}_{t}^{\pi_{0}}\right\rVert,\left\lVert\mathbf{u}_{t}^{\pi_{0}}\right\rVert\leq\kappa^{3}\kappa_{C}W/\gamma$ , we have that $\left\lVert\mathbf{y}_{t}^{\pi_{0}}\right\rVert,\left\lVert\mathbf{u}_{t}^{\pi_{0}}\right\rVert,\left\lVert\mathbf{y}_{t}^{\pi_{T+1}}\right\rVert,\left\lVert\mathbf{u}_{t}^{\pi_{T+1}}\right\rVert\leq 2\kappa^{3}\kappa_{C}W/\gamma$ . Using lipschitzness, this gives us

$$ \displaystyle\sum_{t=1}^{T}\left|c_{t}(\mathbf{y}_{t}^{\pi_{T+1}},\mathbf{u}_{t}^{\pi_{T+1}})-c_{t}(\mathbf{y}_{t}^{\pi_{0}},\mathbf{u}_{t}^{\pi_{0}})\right| \displaystyle\leq\frac{2G\kappa^{3}\kappa_{C}W}{\gamma}\left(\sum_{t=1}^{T}\left\lVert\mathbf{y}_{t}^{\pi_{T+1}}-\mathbf{y}_{t}^{\pi_{0}}\right\rVert+\left\lVert\mathbf{u}_{t}^{\pi_{T+1}}-\mathbf{u}_{t}^{\pi_{0}}\right\rVert\right) \displaystyle\leq\frac{2G\kappa^{3}\kappa_{C}W}{\gamma}\cdot T\cdot 28\kappa^{6}\kappa_{B}^{2}\kappa_{C}^{3}\delta_{1}T \displaystyle\leq\frac{56G\kappa^{9}\kappa_{B}^{2}\kappa_{C}^{4}W}{\gamma}\cdot\delta_{1}T^{2}=\varepsilon T $$

by picking $\delta_{1}=\varepsilon\gamma/56G\kappa^{9}\kappa_{B}^{2}\kappa_{C}^{4}WT\leq W/14\kappa^{3}\kappa_{B}^{2}\kappa_{C}^{2}\gamma T$ . This completes the proof by substituting the value of $\delta_{1}$ into the choosen expressions of $m$ and $h$ .

∎

### A.2 Linear controllers

In the previous section, we have proven that any LDC controller in $\tilde{\mathcal{S}}$ can be approximated by spectral-projection linear controller. As explained previously, this spectral-projection linear controller can be viewed as a linear controller over the lifted system defined in eqns (7), (8), (9).

In this section, we prove that the class of linear controllers can be approximated by spectral filtering. We begin by making certain assumptions only for this section, and defining the class of linear controllers that we aim to compete against and the class of spectral controllers.

#### Assumption A.6.

The system matrices $B,C$ are bounded, i.e., $\|B\|\leq\tilde{\kappa}_{B},\left\lVert C\right\rVert\leq\tilde{\kappa}_{C}$ . The disturbance at each time step is also bounded, i.e., $\|\mathbf{w}_{t}\|\leq\tilde{W}$ .

#### Assumption A.7.

The cost functions $c_{t}(\mathbf{y},\mathbf{u})$ are convex. Moreover, as long as $\|\mathbf{y}\|,\|\mathbf{u}\|\leq D$ , the gradients are bounded:

$$ \|\nabla_{\mathbf{y}}c_{t}(\mathbf{y},\mathbf{u})\|,\|\nabla_{\mathbf{u}}c_{t}(\mathbf{y},\mathbf{u})\|\leq\tilde{G}D\,. $$

#### Definition A.8.

A linear policy $K$ is $(\tilde{\kappa},\tilde{\gamma})$ -diagonalizably stable if there exist matrices $L,H$ satisfying $A+BKC=HLH^{-1}$ , such that the following conditions hold:

- 1. $L$ is diagonal with nonnegative entries.

- 2. The spectral norm of $L$ is strictly less than one, i.e., $\|L\|\leq 1-\tilde{\gamma}$ .

- 3. The controller and the transformation matrices are bounded, i.e., $\|K\|,\|H\|,\|H^{-1}\|\leq\tilde{\kappa}$ .

We denote by $\tilde{\mathcal{S}}=\{K:K\text{ is }(\tilde{\kappa},\tilde{\gamma})\text{-diagonalizably stable}\}$ the set of such policies, and, with slight abuse of notation, also use $\tilde{\mathcal{S}}$ to refer to the class of linear policies $\mathbf{u}_{t}=S\mathbf{y}_{t}$ where $S\in\tilde{\mathcal{S}}$ . Each policy in $\tilde{\mathcal{S}}$ is fully parameterized by the matrix $K\in{\mathbb{R}}^{n\times p}$ .

#### Assumption A.9.

The zero policy $K=0$ lies in $\tilde{\mathcal{S}}$ .

For simplicity, we assume that $\tilde{\kappa},\tilde{\kappa}_{B},\tilde{W},\tilde{G}\geq 1$ and $\tilde{\gamma}\leq 2/3$ , without loss of generality.

We define $\mathbf{y}^{\sf nat}_{t}$ as the observation at time $t$ assuming that all inputs to the system were zero from the beginning of time, i.e.

$$ \mathbf{x}^{\sf nat}_{t+1}=A\mathbf{x}^{\sf nat}_{t}+\mathbf{w}_{t};\quad\quad\quad\quad\mathbf{y}^{\sf nat}_{t}=C\mathbf{x}^{\sf nat}_{t} $$

We define our disturbance response controller with respect to these as follows:

#### Definition A.10.

[Spectral Controller] The class of Spectral Controllers with $h$ parameters, memory $m$ and stability $\tilde{\gamma}$ is defined as:

$$ \displaystyle\left\{\mathbf{u}_{t}^{M}=M_{0}\mathbf{y}^{\sf nat}_{t}+\sum_{i=1}^{h}\lambda_{i}^{1/4}M_{i}Y^{\sf nat}_{t-1:t-m}\boldsymbol{\varphi}_{i}\right\}\,, $$

where $\boldsymbol{\varphi}_{i}\in{\mathbb{R}}^{m},\lambda_{i}\in{\mathbb{R}}$ are the $i^{\sf th}$ top eigenvector and eigenvalue of $H\in{\mathbb{R}}^{m\times m}$ such that $H_{ij}=\frac{\left(1-\tilde{\gamma}\right)^{i+j-1}}{i+j-1}$ . Any policy in this class is fully parameterized by the matrices $M\in{\mathbb{R}}^{n\times p\times h}$ .

The sequence $\{\mathbf{y}^{\sf nat}_{t}\}_{t\in[T]}$ can be iteratively computed using the following:

$$ \mathbf{y}^{\sf nat}_{t}=\mathbf{y}_{t}-C\sum_{i=1}^{t}A^{i-1}B\mathbf{u}_{t-i} $$

Alternatively, it can be carried out recursively, starting from $\mathbf{z}_{0}=0$ , as:

$$ \mathbf{z}_{t+1}=A\mathbf{z}_{t}+B\mathbf{u}_{t};\quad\quad\quad\quad\mathbf{y}^{\sf nat}_{t}=\mathbf{y}_{t}-C\mathbf{z}_{t} $$

#### Lemma A.11.

Under our assumptions, $\left\lVert\mathbf{y}^{\sf nat}_{t}\right\rVert\leq\frac{\tilde{\kappa}^{2}\tilde{\kappa}_{C}\tilde{W}}{\tilde{\gamma}}$

#### Proof.

Unrolling the recursion, we get that

$$ \mathbf{y}_{t}^{\sf nat}=\sum_{i=1}^{t}CA^{i-1}\mathbf{w}_{t-i} $$

Taking norm on both sides,

$$ \displaystyle\left\lVert\mathbf{y}_{t}^{\sf nat}\right\rVert\leq\tilde{\kappa}^{2}\tilde{\kappa}_{C}\tilde{W}\sum_{i=1}^{t}(1-\tilde{\gamma})^{i-1}\leq\frac{\tilde{\kappa}^{2}\tilde{\kappa}_{C}\tilde{W}}{\tilde{\gamma}} $$

∎

#### Lemma A.12.

For any $K\in\tilde{\mathcal{S}}$ , the corresponding states $\mathbf{x}_{t}^{K}$ and control inputs $\mathbf{u}_{t}^{K}$ are bounded by

$$ \displaystyle\left\lVert\mathbf{y}^{K}_{t}\right\rVert\leq\frac{2\tilde{\kappa}^{5}\tilde{\kappa}_{B}\tilde{\kappa}_{C}^{2}\tilde{W}}{\tilde{\gamma}^{2}}\,,\quad\left\lVert\mathbf{u}^{K}_{t}\right\rVert\leq\frac{2\tilde{\kappa}^{6}\tilde{\kappa}_{B}\tilde{\kappa}_{C}^{2}\tilde{W}}{\tilde{\gamma}^{2}}\,. $$

#### Proof.

As in many other parts of this paper, we first write $\Delta_{t}^{K}$ as a linear transformation of nature’s observations:

$$ \displaystyle\left\lVert\Delta_{t}^{K}\right\rVert \displaystyle=\left\lVert\sum_{i=1}^{t}\left(A+BKC\right)^{i-1}BK\mathbf{y}^{\sf nat}_{t-i}\right\rVert \displaystyle\leq\tilde{\kappa}^{3}\tilde{\kappa}_{B}\sum_{i=0}^{t}\left(1-\tilde{\gamma}\right)^{i}\left\lVert\mathbf{y}^{\sf nat}_{t-i-1}\right\rVert \displaystyle\leq\frac{\tilde{\kappa}^{5}\tilde{\kappa}_{B}\tilde{\kappa}_{C}\tilde{W}}{\tilde{\gamma}^{2}}\,. $$

Then, since $\mathbf{y}_{t}^{K}=\mathbf{y}_{t}^{\sf nat}+C\Delta_{t}^{K}$ and $\mathbf{u}_{t}^{K}=K\mathbf{y}_{t}^{K}$ , we get our result. ∎

For convenience of notation, for a given policy $\pi$ we define $\Delta_{t}^{\pi}=\mathbf{x}_{t}^{\pi}-\mathbf{x}_{t}^{{\sf nat}}$ . We begin by defining the class of open-loop optimal controllers as follows:

#### Definition A.13 (Open Loop Optimal Controller).

The class of Open Loop Optimal Controllers of with memory $m$ is defined as:

$$ \displaystyle\left\{\mathbf{u}_{t}^{K,m}=K\mathbf{y}^{\sf nat}_{t}+\sum_{i=1}^{m}KC\left(A+BKC\right)^{i-1}BK\mathbf{y}^{\sf nat}_{t-i}\right\}\,. $$

Any policy in this class is fully parameterized by the matrix $K\in{\mathbb{R}}^{d\times n}$ and the memory $m\in\mathbb{Z}$ .

Next, we state and prove Lemma A.14, which shows that any linear policy in $\tilde{\mathcal{S}}$ can be approximated up to arbitrary accuracy with an open-loop optimal controller of suitable memory.

#### Lemma A.14.

Let a linear policy $K\in\tilde{\mathcal{S}}$ . Then, for $m\geq\frac{1}{\tilde{\gamma}}\log\left(\frac{6\tilde{G}\tilde{\kappa}^{14}\tilde{\kappa}_{B}^{3}\tilde{\kappa}_{C}^{5}\tilde{W}^{2}}{\varepsilon\tilde{\gamma}^{5}}\right)$ and $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\sum_{t=1}^{T}\left|c_{t}(\mathbf{y}_{t}^{K,m},\mathbf{u}_{t}^{K,m})-c_{t}(\mathbf{y}_{t}^{K},\mathbf{u}_{t}^{K})\right|\leq\varepsilon T\,,\quad\quad\quad\quad\left\lVert\mathbf{y}_{t}^{K,m}\right\rVert,\left\lVert\mathbf{u}_{t}^{K,m}\right\rVert\leq\frac{3\tilde{\kappa}^{6}\tilde{\kappa}_{B}\tilde{\kappa}_{C}^{2}\tilde{W}}{\tilde{\gamma}^{2}}\,. $$

#### Proof.

We begin by bounding the difference in the observation and the difference in the control inputs. The difference in cost is bounded using the fact that the cost functions are lipschitz in the control and observation. We begin by unrolling the expressions for $\Delta_{t}^{K}$ in terms of $\mathbf{y}^{\sf nat}_{t}$ :

$$ \displaystyle\Delta_{t}^{K}=A\Delta_{t-1}^{K}+BK\mathbf{y}_{t-1}^{K}=(A+BKC)\Delta_{t-1}^{K}+BK\mathbf{y}_{t-1}^{\sf nat}=\sum_{i=1}^{t}(A+BKC)^{i-1}BK\mathbf{y}^{\sf nat}_{t-i} $$

This gives us that:

$$ \displaystyle\mathbf{u}_{t}^{K}=K\mathbf{y}_{t}^{\sf nat}+KC\Delta_{t}^{K}=K\mathbf{y}_{t}^{\sf nat}+\sum_{i=1}^{t}KC(A+BKC)^{i-1}BK\mathbf{y}^{\sf nat}_{t-i} $$

Notice that for all $t\leq m$ , $\mathbf{u}_{t}^{K}=\mathbf{u}_{t}^{K,m}$ and hence $\mathbf{y}_{t}^{K}=\mathbf{y}_{t}^{K,m}$ . For $t>m$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\left\lVert\mathbf{u}_{t}^{K}-\mathbf{u}_{t}^{K,m}\right\rVert \displaystyle=\left\lVert\sum_{i=m+1}^{t}KC(A+BKC)^{i-1}BK\mathbf{y}^{\sf nat}_{t-i}\right\rVert \displaystyle\leq\frac{\tilde{\kappa}^{6}\tilde{\kappa}_{B}\tilde{\kappa}_{C}^{2}\tilde{W}}{\tilde{\gamma}}\sum_{i=m+1}^{t}(1-\tilde{\gamma})^{i-1} \displaystyle[\Delta-\mbox{ineq., C-S}] \displaystyle\leq\frac{\tilde{\kappa}^{6}\tilde{\kappa}_{B}\tilde{\kappa}_{C}^{2}\tilde{W}}{\tilde{\gamma}^{2}}(1-\tilde{\gamma})^{m}\,. $$

We also note that for any policy $\pi$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\mathbf{y}_{t}^{\pi}=\mathbf{y}_{t}^{\sf nat}+C\Delta_{t}^{\pi}=\mathbf{y}_{t}^{\sf nat}+\sum_{i=1}^{t}CA^{i-1}B\mathbf{u}_{t-i}^{\pi} $$

Using both the previous results and the fact that $\mathbf{u}_{t}^{K}=\mathbf{u}_{t}^{K,m}$ for any $t\leq m$ , we similarly get:

$$ \displaystyle\left\lVert\mathbf{y}_{t}^{K}-\mathbf{y}_{t}^{K,m}\right\rVert=\left\lVert\sum_{i=1}^{t}CA^{i-1}B(\mathbf{u}_{t-i}^{K}-\mathbf{u}_{t-i}^{K,m})\right\rVert=\left\lVert\sum_{i=1}^{t-m}CA^{i-1}B(\mathbf{u}_{t-i}^{K}-\mathbf{u}_{t-i}^{K,m})\right\rVert\,, $$

and by using Assumption A.9 we can write:

$$ \displaystyle\left\lVert\mathbf{y}_{t}^{K}-\mathbf{y}_{t}^{K,m}\right\rVert\leq\tilde{\kappa}_{B}\tilde{\kappa}_{C}\tilde{\kappa}^{2}\sum_{i=1}^{\infty}(1-\tilde{\gamma})^{i-1}\left\lVert\mathbf{u}_{t-i}^{K}-\mathbf{u}_{t-i}^{K,m}\right\rVert\leq\frac{\tilde{\kappa}^{8}\tilde{\kappa}_{B}^{2}\tilde{\kappa}_{C}^{3}\tilde{W}}{\tilde{\gamma}^{3}}(1-\tilde{\gamma})^{m}\,. $$

Using the fact that $\tilde{\kappa}_{B}\tilde{\kappa}_{C}\tilde{\kappa}^{2}/\tilde{\gamma}>1$ , we get the following uniform bound:

$$ \displaystyle\max\left\{\left\lVert\mathbf{u}_{t}^{K}-\mathbf{u}_{t}^{K,m}\right\rVert,\left\lVert\mathbf{y}_{t}^{K}-\mathbf{y}_{t}^{K,m}\right\rVert\right\}\leq\frac{\tilde{\kappa}^{8}\tilde{\kappa}_{B}^{2}\tilde{\kappa}_{C}^{3}\tilde{W}}{\tilde{\gamma}^{3}}(1-\tilde{\gamma})^{m}\,. $$

Whenever $m\geq\frac{1}{\tilde{\gamma}}\log\left(\frac{\tilde{\kappa}^{2}\tilde{\kappa}_{B}\tilde{\kappa}_{C}}{\tilde{\gamma}}\right)$ , which is indeed true from our choice of $\varepsilon$ and $m$ , this implies that the $\left\lVert\mathbf{y}_{t}^{K}-\mathbf{y}_{t}^{K,m}\right\rVert,\left\lVert\mathbf{u}_{t}^{K}-\mathbf{u}_{t}^{K,m}\right\rVert\leq\tilde{\kappa}^{6}\tilde{\kappa}_{B}\tilde{\kappa}_{C}^{2}\tilde{W}/\tilde{\gamma}^{2}$ . Using Lemma A.12 $\left\lVert\mathbf{y}_{t}^{K}\right\rVert,\left\lVert\mathbf{u}_{t}^{K}\right\rVert\leq 2\tilde{\kappa}^{6}\tilde{\kappa}_{B}\tilde{\kappa}_{C}^{2}\tilde{W}/\tilde{\gamma}^{2}$ , by triangle inequality $\left\lVert\mathbf{y}_{t}^{K,m}\right\rVert,\left\lVert\mathbf{u}_{t}^{K,m}\right\rVert\leq 3\tilde{\kappa}^{6}\tilde{\kappa}_{B}\tilde{\kappa}_{C}^{2}\tilde{W}/\tilde{\gamma}^{2}$ . Thus, the sum of costs is bounded using lipschitzness of $c_{t}$ as follows:

$$ \displaystyle\sum_{t=1}^{T}\left|c_{t}(\mathbf{y}_{t}^{K},\mathbf{u}_{t}^{K})-c_{t}(\mathbf{y}_{t}^{K,m},\mathbf{u}_{t}^{K,m})\right| \displaystyle\leq\frac{3\tilde{G}\tilde{\kappa}^{6}\tilde{\kappa}_{B}\tilde{\kappa}_{C}^{2}\tilde{W}}{\tilde{\gamma}^{2}}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\left(\left\lVert\mathbf{y}_{t}^{K}-\mathbf{y}_{t}^{K,m}\right\rVert+\left\lVert\mathbf{u}_{t}^{K}-\mathbf{u}_{t}^{K,m}\right\rVert\right) \displaystyle\leq\frac{6\tilde{G}\tilde{\kappa}^{14}\tilde{\kappa}_{B}^{3}\tilde{\kappa}_{C}^{5}\tilde{W}^{2}}{\tilde{\gamma}^{5}}(1-\tilde{\gamma})^{m}\cdot T\leq\varepsilon T\,. \displaystyle[\mbox{choice of }m] $$

∎

To enable learning via online gradient descent, we require a bounded set of parameters:

#### Definition A.15.

The set of bounded spectral parameters is defined as

$$ {\mathcal{K}}=\left\{M\in{\mathbb{R}}^{h\times n\times p}\mid\left\lVert\mathbf{y}_{t}^{M}\right\rVert,\left\lVert\mathbf{u}_{t}^{M}\right\rVert\leq\frac{4\tilde{\kappa}^{6}\tilde{\kappa}_{B}\tilde{\kappa}_{C}^{2}\tilde{W}}{\tilde{\gamma}^{2}},\left\lVert M_{0}\right\rVert\leq\tilde{\kappa},\left\lVert M_{i}\right\rVert\leq\tilde{\kappa}^{4}\tilde{\kappa}_{B}\tilde{\kappa}_{C}\sqrt{\frac{2}{\tilde{\gamma}}}\right\}\,. $$

We shall now prove that every open-loop optimal controller can be approximated up to arbitrary accuracy with a spectral controller.

#### Lemma A.16.

For every open loop optimal controller $\pi_{K,m}^{\sf OLOC}$ such that $K\in\tilde{\mathcal{S}}$ and $\left\lVert\mathbf{y}^{K,m}\right\rVert,\left\lVert\mathbf{u}^{K,m}\right\rVert\leq\frac{3\tilde{\kappa}^{6}\tilde{\kappa}_{B}\tilde{\kappa}_{C}^{2}\tilde{W}}{\tilde{\gamma}^{2}}$ , there exists an spectral controller $\pi_{h,m,\tilde{\gamma},M}^{\sf SC}$ with $M\in{\mathcal{K}}$ such that:

$$ \displaystyle\sum_{t=1}^{T}\left|c_{t}(\mathbf{y}_{t}^{M},\mathbf{u}_{t}^{M})-c_{t}(\mathbf{y}_{t}^{K,m},\mathbf{u}_{t}^{K,m})\right|\leq\varepsilon T\,. $$

for any $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$ and $h\geq 2\log T\log\left(\frac{400\tilde{G}\tilde{\kappa}^{14}\tilde{\kappa}_{B}^{3}\tilde{\kappa}_{C}^{5}\tilde{W}^{2}\sqrt{m}d}{\varepsilon\tilde{\gamma}^{9/2}}\log T\log^{1/4}\left(\frac{2}{\tilde{\gamma}}\right)\right)$ .

#### Proof.

Since $K\in\tilde{\mathcal{S}}$ , there exists a diagonal $L\in{\mathbb{R}}^{n\times n}$ as in Definition A.8 so that:

$$ \displaystyle\mathbf{u}_{t}^{K,m} \displaystyle=K\mathbf{y}^{\sf nat}_{t}+\sum_{i=1}^{m}KC(A+BKC)^{i-1}BK\mathbf{y}^{\sf nat}_{t-i}=K\mathbf{y}^{\sf nat}_{t}+\sum_{i=1}^{m}KCHL^{i-1}H^{-1}BK\mathbf{y}^{\sf nat}_{t-i}\,. $$

Then write $L^{i-1}=\sum_{j=1}^{d}\alpha_{j}^{i-1}e_{j}e_{j}^{\top}$ and obtain

$$ \displaystyle\mathbf{u}_{t}^{K,m} \displaystyle=K\mathbf{y}^{\sf nat}_{t}+\sum_{i=1}^{m}KCH\left(\sum_{j=1}^{d}\alpha_{j}^{i-1}e_{j}e_{j}^{\top}\right)H^{-1}BK\mathbf{y}^{\sf nat}_{t-i} \displaystyle=K\mathbf{y}^{\sf nat}_{t}+\sum_{j=1}^{d}KCHe_{j}e_{j}^{\top}H^{-1}BK\sum_{i=1}^{m}\alpha_{j}^{i-1}\mathbf{y}^{\sf nat}_{t-i}\,. $$

Recall $Y^{\sf nat}_{t-1:t-m}=[\mathbf{y}^{\sf nat}_{t-1},\dots,\mathbf{y}^{\sf nat}_{t-m}]\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times m}$ , define $\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\alpha}=[1,\alpha,\dots,\alpha^{m-1}]\in{\mathbb{R}}^{m}$ and get

$$ \displaystyle\mathbf{u}_{t}^{K,m} \displaystyle=K\mathbf{y}^{\sf nat}_{t}+\sum_{j=1}^{d}KCHe_{j}e_{j}^{\top}H^{-1}BKY^{\sf nat}_{t-1:t-m}\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\alpha_{j}} \displaystyle=K\mathbf{y}^{\sf nat}_{t}+\sum_{j=1}^{d}KCHe_{j}e_{j}^{\top}H^{-1}BKY^{\sf nat}_{t-1:t-m}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{m}\boldsymbol{\varphi}_{i}\boldsymbol{\varphi}_{i}^{\top}\right)\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\alpha_{j}} \displaystyle\left[\sum_{i=1}^{m}\boldsymbol{\varphi}_{i}\boldsymbol{\varphi}_{i}^{\top}=\mathbb{I}_{m}\right] \displaystyle=K\mathbf{y}^{\sf nat}_{t}+\sum_{i=1}^{m}\left(\sum_{j=1}^{d}KCHe_{j}e_{j}^{\top}H^{-1}BK\boldsymbol{\varphi}_{i}^{\top}\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\alpha_{j}}\right)Y^{\sf nat}_{t-1:t-m}\boldsymbol{\varphi}_{i}\,. $$

Let $\pi_{h,m,\tilde{\gamma},M^{*}}^{\sf SC}$ be the spectral controller with $M_{0}=K$ and $M^{*}_{i}=\lambda_{i}^{-1/4}KCH\left(\sum_{j=1}^{d}\boldsymbol{\varphi}_{i}^{\top}\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\alpha_{j}}e_{j}e_{j}^{\top}\right)H^{-1}BK$ for all $i\in[h]$ . Note that we have

$$ \displaystyle\left\lVert M_{0}\right\rVert\leq\tilde{\kappa},\quad\left\lVert M^{*}_{i}\right\rVert\leq\tilde{\kappa}^{4}\tilde{\kappa}_{B}\tilde{\kappa}_{C}\cdot\max_{\ell\in[d]}\lambda_{j}^{-1/4}\left<\boldsymbol{\varphi}_{j},\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\alpha_{l}}\right>\quad\forall 1\leq j\leq m\,, $$

and from the analysis of Lemma 7.4 of [7], we have that $\lambda_{j}^{-1/4}\left<\boldsymbol{\varphi}_{j},\mu(\alpha_{l})\right>\leq\sqrt{\frac{2}{\tilde{\gamma}}}$ . Thus, $\left\lVert M^{*}_{i}\right\rVert\leq\tilde{\kappa}^{4}\tilde{\kappa}_{B}\tilde{\kappa}_{C}\sqrt{\frac{2}{\tilde{\gamma}}}$ . Then,

$$ \displaystyle\left\lVert\mathbf{u}_{t}^{K,m}-\mathbf{u}_{t}^{M^{*}}\right\rVert \displaystyle=\left\lVert\sum_{i=h+1}^{m}KCH\left(\sum_{j=1}^{d}\boldsymbol{\varphi}_{i}^{\top}\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\alpha_{j}}e_{j}e_{j}^{\top}\right)H^{-1}BKY^{\sf nat}_{t-1:t-m}\boldsymbol{\varphi}_{i}\right\rVert \displaystyle\leq\frac{\tilde{\kappa}^{6}\tilde{\kappa}_{B}\tilde{\kappa}_{C}^{2}\tilde{W}\sqrt{m}}{\tilde{\gamma}}\sum_{i=h+1}^{m}\sum_{j=1}^{d}|\boldsymbol{\varphi}_{i}^{\top}\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\alpha_{j}}| \displaystyle\left[\left\lVert Y_{t-1:t-m}\right\rVert\leq\frac{\tilde{\kappa}^{2}\tilde{\kappa}_{C}\tilde{W}}{\tilde{\gamma}}\sqrt{m}\right] \displaystyle\leq\frac{30\tilde{\kappa}^{6}\tilde{\kappa}_{B}\tilde{\kappa}_{C}^{2}\tilde{W}\sqrt{m}}{\tilde{\gamma}^{3/2}}\log^{1/4}\left(\frac{2}{\tilde{\gamma}}\right)\sum_{i=h+1}^{m}\sum_{j=1}^{d}\exp\left(-\frac{\pi^{2}j}{16\log T}\right) \displaystyle\left[\text{Lemma 7.4 of \cite[cite]{[\@@bibref{Number}{brahmbhatt2025newapproachcontrollinglinear}{}{}]}}\right] \displaystyle\leq\frac{30\tilde{\kappa}^{6}\tilde{\kappa}_{B}\tilde{\kappa}_{C}^{2}\tilde{W}\sqrt{m}d}{\tilde{\gamma}^{3/2}}\log^{1/4}\left(\frac{2}{\tilde{\gamma}}\right)\intop_{h}^{\infty}\exp\left(-\frac{\pi^{2}j}{16\log T}\right)dx \displaystyle\leq\frac{50\tilde{\kappa}^{6}\tilde{\kappa}_{B}\tilde{\kappa}_{C}^{2}\tilde{W}\sqrt{m}d}{\tilde{\gamma}^{3/2}}\log T\log^{1/4}\left(\frac{2}{\tilde{\gamma}}\right)\exp\left({-\frac{\pi^{2}h}{16\log T}}\right)\,, $$

$$ \displaystyle\left\lVert\mathbf{y}_{t}^{M^{*}}-\mathbf{y}_{t}^{K,m}\right\rVert \displaystyle=\left\lVert\sum_{i=1}^{t}CA^{i-1}B(\mathbf{u}_{t-i}^{M^{*}}-\mathbf{u}_{t-i}^{K,m})\right\rVert \displaystyle\leq\tilde{\kappa}_{B}\tilde{\kappa}_{C}\tilde{\kappa}^{2}\sum_{i=1}^{t}(1-\tilde{\gamma})^{i-1}\left\lVert\mathbf{u}_{t-i}^{M}-\mathbf{u}_{t-i}^{K,m}\right\rVert \displaystyle[\mbox{Assumption \ref{asm:zero-stabilizable-system}}] \displaystyle\leq\frac{50\tilde{\kappa}^{8}\tilde{\kappa}_{B}^{2}\tilde{\kappa}_{C}^{3}\tilde{W}\sqrt{m}d}{\tilde{\gamma}^{5/2}}\log T\log^{1/4}\left(\frac{2}{\tilde{\gamma}}\right)\exp\left({-\frac{\pi^{2}h}{16\log T}}\right)\,. $$

Using the fact that $\tilde{\kappa}_{C}\tilde{\kappa}_{B}\tilde{\kappa}^{2}/\tilde{\gamma}>1$ , we get a uniform bound:

$$ \displaystyle\max\left\{\left\lVert\mathbf{y}_{t}^{K,m}-\mathbf{y}_{t}^{M^{*}}\right\rVert,\left\lVert\mathbf{u}_{t}^{K,m}-\mathbf{u}_{t}^{M^{*}}\right\rVert\right\}\leq\frac{50\tilde{\kappa}^{8}\tilde{\kappa}_{B}^{2}\tilde{\kappa}_{C}^{3}\tilde{W}\sqrt{m}d}{\tilde{\gamma}^{5/2}}\log T\log^{1/4}\left(\frac{2}{\tilde{\gamma}}\right)\exp\left({-\frac{\pi^{2}h}{16\log T}}\right)\,. $$

Whenever $h\geq 2\log T\log\left(\frac{50\tilde{\kappa}_{B}\tilde{\kappa}_{C}\tilde{\kappa}^{2}\sqrt{m}d}{\sqrt{\tilde{\gamma}}}\log T\log\left(\frac{2}{\tilde{\gamma}}\right)\right)$ , which is indeed the case for our choice of $\varepsilon$ and $h$ , this implies that $\left\lVert\mathbf{y}_{t}^{M^{*}}-\mathbf{y}_{t}^{K,m}\right\rVert,\left\lVert\mathbf{u}_{t}^{M^{*}}-\mathbf{u}_{t}^{K,m}\right\rVert\leq\frac{\tilde{\kappa}^{6}\tilde{\kappa}_{B}\tilde{\kappa}_{C}^{2}\tilde{W}}{\tilde{\gamma}^{2}}$ . Hence, by triangle inequality $\left\lVert\mathbf{y}_{t}^{M^{*}}\right\rVert,\left\lVert\mathbf{u}_{t}^{M^{*}}\right\rVert\leq\frac{4\tilde{\kappa}^{6}\tilde{\kappa}_{B}\tilde{\kappa}_{C}^{2}\tilde{W}}{\tilde{\gamma}^{2}}$ . Thus, the sum of costs is bounded as follows:

$$ \displaystyle\sum_{t=1}^{T}\left|c_{t}(\mathbf{y}_{t}^{M^{*}},\mathbf{u}_{t}^{M^{*}})-c_{t}(\mathbf{y}_{t}^{K,m},\mathbf{u}_{t}^{K,m})\right| \displaystyle\leq\frac{4\tilde{G}\tilde{\kappa}^{6}\tilde{\kappa}_{B}\tilde{\kappa}_{C}^{2}\tilde{W}}{\tilde{\gamma}^{2}}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\left(\left\lVert\mathbf{y}_{t}^{M^{*}}-\mathbf{y}_{t}^{K,m}\right\rVert+\left\lVert\mathbf{u}_{t}^{M^{*}}-\mathbf{u}_{t}^{K,m}\right\rVert\right) \displaystyle\leq\frac{400\tilde{G}\tilde{\kappa}^{14}\tilde{\kappa}_{B}^{3}\tilde{\kappa}_{C}^{5}\tilde{W}^{2}\sqrt{m}d}{\tilde{\gamma}^{9/2}}\log T\log^{1/4}\left(\frac{2}{\tilde{\gamma}}\right)\exp\left({-\frac{\pi^{2}h}{16\log T}}\right)\cdot T \displaystyle\leq\varepsilon T\,.\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad[\mbox{choice of }h] $$

∎

Using these lemmas, we complete the proof of Lemma A.3 as follows:

#### Proof of Lemma A.3.

The proof follows directly from Lemmas A.14 and A.16. ∎

## Appendix B Learning Results

### B.1 Convexity of loss function and feasibility set

To conclude the analysis, we first show that the feasibility set ${\mathcal{K}}$ is convex and the loss functions are convex with respect to the variables $M$ . This follows since the states and the controls are linear transformations of the variables.

#### Lemma B.1.

The set ${\mathcal{K}}$ from Definition 3.7 is convex.

#### Proof.

Since $\mathbf{x}_{t}^{M},\mathbf{u}_{t}^{M}$ are linear in $M$ , from the convexity of the norm, the fact that the sublevel sets of a convex function is convex and that the intersection of convex sets is convex, we are done. ∎

#### Lemma B.2.

The loss $\ell_{t}(M)$ is convex in $M$ .

#### Proof.

The loss function $\ell_{t}$ is given by $\ell_{t}(M)=c_{t}(\mathbf{x}_{t}(M),\mathbf{u}_{t}(M)).$ Since the cost $c_{t}$ is a convex function with respect to its arguments, we simply need to show that $\mathbf{x}_{t}^{M}$ and $\mathbf{u}_{t}^{M}$ depend linearly on $M$ . The control is given by

$$ \displaystyle\mathbf{u}_{t}^{M}= \displaystyle\bar{M}_{0}\mathbf{y}^{\sf nat}_{t}+\sum_{i=1}^{\tilde{h}}\sum_{j=1}^{\tilde{m}}\lambda_{i}^{1/4}\left[\varphi_{i}\right]_{j}\bar{M}_{i}\mathbf{y}_{t-j}^{\sf nat}+\sum_{l=0}^{h}\sum_{k=0}^{m}\sigma_{l}^{1/4}\left[\phi_{l}\right]_{k}M_{0l}\mathbf{y}_{t-k}^{\sf nat} \displaystyle\quad+\sum_{i=1}^{\tilde{h}}\sum_{j=1}^{\tilde{m}}\sum_{l=0}^{h}\sum_{k=0}^{m}\left(\sigma_{l}\lambda_{i}\right)^{1/4}\left[\phi_{l}\right]_{k}\left[\varphi_{i}\right]_{j}M_{il}\mathbf{y}_{t-j-k}^{\sf nat}\,, $$

which is a linear function of the variables. Similarly, the observation $\mathbf{y}_{t}^{M}$ is given by

$$ \mathbf{y}_{t}^{M}=\mathbf{y}_{t}^{\sf nat}+\sum_{q=1}^{t}CA^{q-1}B\mathbf{u}_{t-q}^{M}\,. $$

Thus, we have shown that $\mathbf{y}_{t}(M)$ and $\mathbf{u}_{t}(M)$ are linear transformations of $M$ . A composition of convex and linear functions is convex, which concludes our Lemma. ∎

### B.2 Lipschitzness of $\ell_{t}(\cdot)$

The following lemma states and proves the explicit lipschitz constant of $\ell_{t}(\cdot)$ .

#### Lemma B.3.

For any $M,M^{\prime}\in\mathcal{K}$ it holds that,

$$ \displaystyle\left|\ell_{t}(M)-\ell_{t}(M^{\prime})\right|\leq\frac{32G\mathcal{R}h\tilde{h}\sqrt{m\tilde{m}}\kappa^{4}\kappa_{B}\kappa_{C}^{2}W}{\gamma^{2}}\log^{1/2}\left(\frac{2}{\gamma}\right)\left\lVert M-M^{\prime}\right\rVert\,. $$

#### Proof.

Taking the difference in controls defined in eqn. (21):

$$ \displaystyle\left\lVert\mathbf{u}_{t}(M)-\mathbf{u}_{t}(M^{\prime})\right\rVert \displaystyle\leq\frac{16h\tilde{h}\sqrt{m\tilde{m}}\kappa^{2}\kappa_{C}W}{\gamma}\log^{1/2}\left(\frac{2}{\gamma}\right)\left\lVert M-M^{\prime}\right\rVert $$

Taking the difference in the observations,

$$ \displaystyle\left\lVert\mathbf{y}_{t}(M)-\mathbf{y}_{t}(M^{\prime})\right\rVert \displaystyle=\left\lVert\sum_{q=1}^{t}CA^{q-1}B(\mathbf{u}_{t-q}(M)-\mathbf{u}_{t-q}(M^{\prime}))\right\rVert \displaystyle\leq\frac{\kappa_{B}\kappa_{C}\kappa^{2}}{\gamma}\max_{q\in[t]}\left\{\left\lVert\mathbf{u}_{t-q}(M)-\mathbf{u}_{t-q}(M^{\prime})\right\rVert\right\} \displaystyle\leq\frac{16h\tilde{h}\sqrt{m\tilde{m}}\kappa^{4}\kappa_{B}\kappa_{C}^{2}W}{\gamma^{2}}\log^{1/2}\left(\frac{2}{\gamma}\right)\left\lVert M-M^{\prime}\right\rVert $$

Using the fact that $\kappa_{B}\kappa_{C}\kappa^{2}/\gamma>1$ , we get a uniform bound:

$$ \displaystyle\max\left\{\left\lVert\mathbf{y}_{t}(M)-\mathbf{y}_{t}(M^{\prime})\right\rVert,\left\lVert\mathbf{u}_{t}(M)-\mathbf{u}_{t}(M^{\prime})\right\rVert\right\}\leq\frac{16h\tilde{h}\sqrt{m\tilde{m}}\kappa^{4}\kappa_{B}\kappa_{C}^{2}W}{\gamma^{2}}\log^{1/2}\left(\frac{2}{\gamma}\right)\left\lVert M-M^{\prime}\right\rVert\,. $$

Using the lipschizness of the cost function from Assumption 3.3, the definition of ${\mathcal{K}}$ , we have

$$ \displaystyle\left|\ell_{t}(M)-\ell_{t}(M^{\prime})\right| \displaystyle=\left|c_{t}(\mathbf{y}_{t}(M),\mathbf{u}_{t}(M))-c_{t}(\mathbf{y}_{t}(M^{\prime}),\mathbf{u}_{t}(M^{\prime}))\right| \displaystyle\leq G\mathcal{R}\left(\left\lVert\mathbf{x}_{t}(M)-\mathbf{x}_{t}(M^{\prime})\right\rVert+\left\lVert\mathbf{u}_{t}(M)-\mathbf{u}_{t}(M^{\prime})\right\rVert\right) \displaystyle\leq\frac{32G\mathcal{R}h\tilde{h}\sqrt{m\tilde{m}}\kappa^{4}\kappa_{B}\kappa_{C}^{2}W}{\gamma^{2}}\log^{1/2}\left(\frac{2}{\gamma}\right)\left\lVert M-M^{\prime}\right\rVert\,. $$

∎

### B.3 Loss functions with memory

The actual loss $c_{t}$ at time $t$ is not calculated on $\mathbf{x}_{t}(M^{t})$ , but rather on the true state $\mathbf{x}_{t}$ , which in turn depends on different parameters $M^{i}$ for various historical times $i<t$ . Nevertheless, $c_{t}(\mathbf{x}_{t},\mathbf{u}_{t})$ is well approximated by $\ell_{t}(M^{t})$ , as stated in Lemma 4.3 and proven next.

Proof of Lemma 4.3: By the choice of step size $\eta$ , and by the computation of the lipschitz constant of $\ell_{t}$ w.r.t $M$ in Lemma B.3, we have:

$$ \eta=\frac{\mathcal{R}_{M}}{L\sqrt{T}}\,, $$

where $L$ is the lipschitz constant of $\ell_{t}$ w.r.t $M$ , computed in Lemma B.3. Thus, for each $j\in[h]$ ,

$$ \|M^{t}-M^{t-i}\|\leq\sum_{s=t-i+1}^{t}\|M^{s}-M^{s-1}\|\leq i\eta L=\frac{i\mathcal{R}_{M}}{\sqrt{T}}\,. $$

Observe that $\mathbf{u}_{t}=\mathbf{u}_{t}(M^{t})$ . Observe that $\mathbf{y}_{t}$ and $\mathbf{y}_{t}(M^{t})$ can be written as

$$ \mathbf{y}_{t}(M^{t})=\sum_{q=1}^{t}CA^{q-1}B\mathbf{u}_{t-q}(M^{t})\,,\quad\quad\mathbf{y}_{t}=\sum_{q=1}^{t}CA^{q-1}B\mathbf{u}_{t-q}(M^{t-q})\,. $$

Evaluating the difference,

$$ \displaystyle\|\mathbf{y}_{t}-\mathbf{y}_{t}(M^{t})\| \displaystyle\leq\left\lVert\sum_{q=1}^{t}CA^{q-1}B(\mathbf{u}_{t-q}(M^{t})-\mathbf{u}_{t-q}(M^{t-q}))\right\rVert \displaystyle\leq\kappa_{B}\kappa_{C}\kappa^{2}\sum_{q=1}^{t}(1-\gamma)^{q-1}\left\lVert\mathbf{u}_{t-q}(M^{t})-\mathbf{u}_{t-q}(M^{t-q})\right\rVert \displaystyle\leq\frac{16h\tilde{h}\sqrt{m\tilde{m}}\kappa^{4}\kappa_{B}\kappa_{C}^{2}W}{\gamma}\log^{1/2}\left(\frac{2}{\gamma}\right)\sum_{q=1}^{t}(1-\gamma)^{q-1}\left\lVert M^{t}-M^{t-q}\right\rVert \displaystyle\leq\frac{16\mathcal{R}_{M}h\tilde{h}\sqrt{m\tilde{m}}\kappa^{4}\kappa_{B}\kappa_{C}^{2}W}{\gamma\sqrt{T}}\log^{1/2}\left(\frac{2}{\gamma}\right)\sum_{q=1}^{t}q(1-\gamma)^{q-1} \displaystyle\leq\frac{16\mathcal{R}_{M}h\tilde{h}\sqrt{m\tilde{m}}\kappa^{4}\kappa_{B}\kappa_{C}^{2}W}{\gamma^{3}\sqrt{T}}\log^{1/2}\left(\frac{2}{\gamma}\right)\,. $$

By definition, $\ell_{t}(M^{t})=c_{t}(\mathbf{y}_{t}(M^{t}),\mathbf{u}_{t}(M^{t}))$ , and by the definition of ${\mathcal{K}}$ and the projection used in Algorithm 1 we have by Assumption 3.3:

$$ \displaystyle\left|\ell_{t}(M^{t})-c_{t}(\mathbf{y}_{t},\mathbf{u}_{t})\right| \displaystyle=\left|c_{t}(\mathbf{y}_{t}(M^{t}),\mathbf{u}_{t}(M^{t}))-c_{t}(\mathbf{y}_{t},\mathbf{u}_{t})\right| \displaystyle\leq G\mathcal{R}\|\mathbf{y}_{t}(M^{t})-\mathbf{y}_{t}\| \displaystyle\leq\frac{16G\mathcal{R}\mathcal{R}_{M}h\tilde{h}\sqrt{m\tilde{m}}\kappa^{4}\kappa_{B}\kappa_{C}^{2}W}{\gamma^{3}\sqrt{T}}\log^{1/2}\left(\frac{2}{\gamma}\right)\,. $$

$\square$

## Appendix C Experiments

We present a series of synthetic experiments designed to evaluate the performance of the DSC, as specified in Algorithm 1. We compare DSC against the gradient response controller (GRC) [22] and the linear quadratic gaussian controller (LQG) [6]. We analyze the performance of these three controllers under the following system settings: a linear signal, where the initial state $\mathbf{x}_{0}$ is randomly sampled from the Gaussian distribution; and a signal with the ReLU state transition. For each signal type, we evaluate the performance of controllers under two types of perturbations: (i) Gaussian noise, and (ii) sinusoidal disturbances; and provide 95% confidence intervals for each setting.

For each experiment, we consider an LDS with a hidden state dimension of $d=10$ , observation dimension of $p=3$ , and a control dimension of $n=2$ . The system matrix $A\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$ is diagonalizable, with the largest eigenvalue being $0.8$ , ensuring marginal stability. The control matrix $B\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times n}$ consists of Normally distributed entries. For the described settings, we use $h=\tilde{h}=5$ filters and $m=\tilde{m}=10$ memory for both controllers.

Each figure reports the average quadratic loss computed over a sliding window, with its size set to 10% of the sequence length. The empirical results presented in Figures 3(a) demonstrate that the DSC controller outperforms the GRC controller, while LQG remains optimal for the setting with Gaussian perturbations. **Authors:** Anand Brahmbhatt ††thanks: Authors ordered alphabetically. ## Abstract

We propose a new method for controlling linear dynamical systems under adversarial disturbances and cost functions. Our algorithm achieves a running time that scales polylogarithmically with the inverse of the stability margin, improving upon prior methods with polynomial dependence maintaining the same regret guarantees. The technique, which may be of independent interest, is based on a novel convex relaxation that approximates linear control policies using spectral filters constructed from the eigenvectors of a specific Hankel matrix.

## 1 Introduction

Controlling linear dynamical systems (LDS) in the presence of adversarial disturbances is a fundamental problem at the intersection of control theory and online learning, with implications for robotics, reinforcement learning, and beyond. Given control inputs $\mathbf{u}_{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{n}$ and disturbances $\mathbf{w}_{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}$ , the system state $\mathbf{x}_{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}$ evolves according to the linear dynamics:

$$ \displaystyle\mathbf{x}_{t+1}=A\mathbf{x}_{t}+B\mathbf{u}_{t}+\mathbf{w}_{t}\,. $$

Given a sequence of cost functions $c_{t}(\mathbf{x}_{t},\mathbf{u}_{t})$ , the goal is to choose control inputs $\mathbf{u}_{t}$ that minimize the cumulative cost.

The classical Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) problem considers known system dynamics and fixed quadratic cost functions. Introduced in the seminal work of Kalman (1960), the optimal control solution assumes that disturbances $\mathbf{w}_{t}$ are drawn i.i.d from a zero-mean distribution. However, this stochastic assumption is often unrealistic in practice, and cost functions may vary arbitrarily over time. In this paper, we address the setting of adversarial noise and more general convex Lipschitz loss functions $c_{t}$ that are adversarially chosen.

This setting falls under the framework of Online Control. For a comprehensive overview, see Hazan and Singh (2025). In this work, we focus on known time-invariant LDS with full observation of the states.

#### Minimizing Regret in Control.

In adversarial settings, minimizing cumulative cost is generally intractable, as the decision maker only observes the loss after choosing the control input. Instead, following the standard approach in online decision making, we aim to compete with the best stationary policy $\pi\in\Pi$ in hindsight. This is captured by the notion of regret, defined as

$$ \displaystyle\text{Regret}_{T}\left(\mathcal{A},\Pi\right)=\sum_{t=1}^{T}c_{t}\left(\mathbf{x}_{t}^{\mathcal{A}},\mathbf{u}_{t}^{\mathcal{A}}\right)-\min_{\pi\in\Pi}\sum_{t=1}^{T}c_{t}\left(\mathbf{x}_{t}^{\pi},\mathbf{u}_{t}^{\pi}\right)\,, $$

where $\mathbf{x}_{t}^{\mathcal{A}}$ is the state induced by the algorithm’s controls $\mathbf{u}_{t}^{\mathcal{A}}$ , and $\mathbf{x}_{t}^{\pi}$ is the state under the fixed policy $\pi$ .

A natural choice for $\Pi$ is the class of linear state-feedback policies $\mathbf{u}_{t}=K\mathbf{x}_{t}$ , standard in control. While optimal in certain settings, finding the best such controller is a nonconvex problem. We therefore adopt improper learning, competing with the best linear policy using a broader class.

To enable efficient learning and analysis, it is common to impose structure on the comparator class—for instance, strong stability (Cohen et al., 2018) or diagonal strong stability (Agarwal et al., 2019b). Following this line, we define in Definition 3.4 the class of diagonalizably stable policies, which preserves sufficient expressiveness for general LDS control. Marginally Stable Comparators: For linear policies $\mathbf{u}_{t}=K\mathbf{x}_{t}$ , stability is determined by the spectral radius $\rho$ of the closed-loop matrix $A+BK$ , with state evolution $\mathbf{x}_{t}=\sum_{i=1}^{t}(A+BK)^{i-1}\mathbf{w}_{t-i}\,.$ While small $\rho$ ensures rapid decay of disturbances, many applications favor marginal stability, where $\rho=1-\gamma$ for small $\gamma$ . This regime preserves long-term memory and yields smoother, more energy-efficient control, useful in settings like robotics, thermal systems, and satellite dynamics. See Section 9 for an example.

### 1.1 Our Contributions

New Control Method: We propose Online Spectral Control (OSC), a new algorithm that controls any controllable LDS by convolving past disturbances with the eigenvectors of a specific Hankel matrix. OSC achieves logarithmic dependence on the stability margin, significantly improving runtime while retaining optimal regret guarantees.

Improved Runtime Dependence: For Algorithm 1, we prove the regret bound

$$ \text{Regret}_{T}\left(\text{OSC}\right)\leq\sqrt{T}/\gamma^{4}\,, $$

where $\gamma$ is the stability margin (Definition 3.4). The runtime scales only polylogarithmically with $1/\gamma$ , improving upon the polynomial dependence in the Gradient Perturbation Controller (GPC) of Agarwal et al.
